source_edition: CC0 1.0 English translation from the modern Amharic EOTC text, Internet Archive item three-books-of-meqabyan-cc0-translation (2026). Not from Ge'ez. Provisional: weigh below KJV, WEB, and Charles.

1.text: Concerning the merciful and meek one who is to come in the latter time, who shall avenge himself against the cruel and deceiving Devil — the opposer of his Creator’s way — the islands of Egypt rejoice.

2.text: And he shall avenge him; for he [the Devil] has exalted himself in his heart; [the avenger] shall return his glory to the earth and to humiliation.

3.text: For he [the Devil] said: “Who is above me? I will enter the depths of the sea; I will ascend to heaven; I will see the deeps; I will grasp the sons of Adam like the chicks of a bird, and I will seize them.

4.text: “That I may turn them away from the straight law of God, I will create occasion against them; I shall prevail over people who live on earth and have not done God’s will; there is none who shall deliver from my hand.

5.text: “And I shall return them to a perverse path, that they may go with me to destruction.

6.text: “Therefore those who love him and keep his law hate me. But those who err, separated from their Lord, come to me; they love me; they keep my covenant. I darken their hearts that they may not return to God their Creator; I twist their thoughts; they do my commandment as I have commanded them.

7.text: “When I show them the wealth of this world, I lead their minds astray from the straight way; when I show them beautiful women and maidens, by these I lead them away.

8.text: “When I show them the gleaming gems of India, gold and silver — that they may turn to my work — by these too I lead them away.

9.text: “When I show them fine clothing, white silk and red silk, brocade and fine linen, by these I lead them away; I return them to my thought. When I show them silver and cattle multiplied as the sand, by this too I return them to my work.

10.text: “Concerning women, anger and quarrel, prideful jealousy — when I show them these, by all this I return them to my way.

11.text: “When I show them signs, I dwell in the mind of their neighbors; in their minds I cause a sign-matter to dwell of itself; I show them the sign of their word and lead them astray.

12.text: “To the people whom I have made my dwelling, I show signs — whether by the motion of stars, or by the rising of clouds, or by the flickering of fire, or by the cries of beasts and birds — they are dwellings; by all this I cause signs to dwell in their mind.

13.text: “They speak and give a sign to their neighbors; and as those diviners told them before, I become their sign.

14.text: “To the people who say to their neighbors, ‘There are no diviners like so-and-so and so-and-so — who, having examined them, give their wage; whose prophecies happen as they spoke; who distinguish evil and good; for whom all comes to pass as they spoke’ — for these, I make the sign of their word.

15.text: “That those who shall perish and those who err in me may utterly multiply, that the sons of Adam may perish with me — when they say this, I am glad. For when I said ‘I will not bow to my inferior,’ God for the sake of their father Adam humbled me from my glory.

16.text: “And I have a covenant with God my Creator: those whom I have deceived, who walk in my commandment, shall be cast with me into the fire.

17.text: “When I had multiplied my arrogance against him, when he had commanded that they bind me and cast me into Gehenna and the depth of Sheol, I petitioned my Lord. When my Creator had so commanded — ‘You have stirred my anger; you have rebuked me with your scourge; you have struck me with your wrath’ — I said, ‘O my Lord, permit me to speak one matter before you,’ and I petitioned in his presence.

18.text: “And my Lord said in reply: ‘Speak, I will hear you.’ At that time I began to petition him thus: ’After I am humbled from my glory, let those whom I have deceived be with me in the affliction I receive.

19.text: “’But those who refused me, who did not err in me, who do your commandment, who fulfill your will, who keep your word — those who would not keep my commandment, who refused me when I tried to teach them, who though I deceived them did not err in me — let them belong to your kingdom; let them take the crown you gave me when you loved me.

20.text: “’Give my crown to the authorities who were not banished with me and not called Satans; in my throne emptied of me and my armies, at your right hand place them.

21.text: “‘As you have desired, let them praise you; let them be as I and as my armies were. For you have hated me, and have loved those created from ash and earth; my authority has been overturned; their authority has been exalted; as you desire, let them praise you.’”

22.text: And my Lord said in reply: “Because, seeing and hearing my work, they have not loved me — but you — let them be according to your desire and your word.

23.text: “If they have left my commandment and the words of the Scriptures and come to you, their destruction does not grieve me. You also, with those you have deceived — shall be punished with you in Gehenna.

24.text: “Forever, for you and those who erred in you, there is no exit from the punishment of Gehenna; rather, forever in fire you shall be tormented.”

1.text: “But you, who could not deceive my servant Job — by honor I will inherit your throne to those of them; those whom you could not deceive, I will give the Kingdom of Heaven — says God who rules all.”

2.text: “And I [the Devil] shall deceive the sons of Adam in all things. If I can deceive them, I shall not leave them to stand firm in good work. I shall deceive all the sons of Adam; I shall make sweet to them the desire of the world.

3.text: “In loving food, in loving drink, in loving clothing — in loving matter, in giving and receiving;

4.text: “in loving hearing and sight; in loving touch and walking; in multiplying pride and matter; in loving sleep and dream;

5.text: “in multiplying drink and drunkenness; in multiplying blasphemy and anger; in speaking jest and joke;

6.text: “in slandering one’s neighbor in quarrel; in seeing the beautiful women of this world; in smelling the perfumes that lead astray —

7.text: “in all this I shall hurl them down, that they may not be saved. Through them, that they may enter with me into the destruction to which I was humbled from my throne, I shall lead them away from the way of God.”

8.text: And the prophet said: “You destroyer and destroyed! In your arrogance and the hardness of your heart — by grieving your Creator and not praising your Creator — when you departed from God’s commandment and denied him, how do you exalt yourself thus over the creation of God?

9.text: “When your Creator was angry with you for your evil work, he cast you down. Why do you take the wretch whom your Creator created from earth and dust, whom he formed as he pleased, whom he set for his praise?

10.text: “You, the subtle one, whom he created from flame of fire and wind, when you exalted yourself, saying ‘I am the Creator’ —

11.text: “and when you boasted, God saw your evil work; that his name might be praised without lack — that one might praise him in your stead — he created Adam. For you, with your armies, had denied God.

12.text: “And Adam and his children were created that they might praise the name of God in your stead — you and your armies who despised God on account of your arrogance — for you had exalted yourself above all the archangels.

13.text: “Therefore God separated you from all archangels like you and humbled you. You — who were created with one counsel together with your armies — for the unprofitable hardness of your mind and the arrogance of your thought, you departed from the praise of God; you erred; you exalted yourself, not against another, but against your Creator.

14.text: “Therefore — that he might be praised by the humble — he created Adam from the earth of the ground. He gave him commandment and law that he should not eat from the fruit of the fig.

15.text: “He appointed him over all he had created. He made known to him thus: ‘Eat from every tree in the Garden; but from the one tree which is the thorn of death, do not eat — lest you bring death upon yourself.’

16.text: “And when you heard this word, upon Eve — who was found from Adam’s rib — you spat the venom of your mouth.

17.text: “That you might make her a law-breaker like yourself, by evil flattery you seized the innocent lamb.

18.text: “When you deceived Eve — who was created as a meek dove, who did not know your cunning — by your prepared matter and your perverse word, you caused her to deny [God]. And after you had deceived that first creature, she went and deceived God’s first earth-creation, Adam.

19.text: “In your pride, you added unbecoming uproar to him; you caused him to deny his Creator’s word; in your pride, you destroyed the poor one.

20.text: “In your cunning, you separated him from his Creator’s love; through your contrivance, you brought him out of the Paradise of joy; through your stumbling-block, you caused him to leave the food of Paradise.

21.text: “In your falsehood, you made him thirst for the drink of Paradise. For from the beginning you have been opposed to the meek Adam — that you might bring him down to the Sheol where you receive your recompense — from his God who loves him, who brought him from non-existence into true existence.

22.text: “Though he was earthly, in soul and flesh and mind he made him spiritual and rational — that he might honor and praise his Creator.

23.text: “As the harp [praises] with many varied modes, he created for him ten Consciousnesses that praise.”

1.text: And his [Adam’s] Lord said: “I shall redeem him; he shall shame you [the Devil]; from the wolf’s mouth he shall save the lamb.

2.text: “But you — leading those you have ruled with you — shall go to destruction.

3.text: “But those who keep their Creator God’s law — that he may make them his portion, that they may praise him with the holy angels who did not transgress their Creator God’s law as you did — these shall be glad with their Creator God, who has hidden them from your evil work.

4.text: “But you — when God, who had chosen you above all those like you, made you praise him together with the angels — in your arrogance you lost the high throne.

5.text: “You exalted yourself; you were called the Devil; your armies were called demons.

6.text: “But those who love God — like the holy angels — become his kindred. The Seraphim and Cherubim who praise him, with wings spread, praise without ceasing.

7.text: “But you — together with your kindred and armies created in your form, who were to praise him always — destroyed your praise through your pride and folly.

8.text: “Thinking that creation was impossible without you — when you forgot the praise of God your Creator — that the praise of God who created you as a tenth tribe might not be lacking — when you separated yourself from the unity of your brothers, that the praise of God might not be lacking,

9.text: “when in the arrogance of your mind you neglected the praise of God your Creator — when he was angry with you and mocked you, when together with your armies he expelled you to the grinding of Gehenna —

10.text: “with his holy hands he took earth from the ground; he added water and fire and wind; and he created Adam in his image and likeness.

11.text: “That his praise might be filled by your deficiency, he appointed him over all the creation he had made with his hand. The earthly praise was joined to the heavenly praise; their praise became equal.

12.text: “But you — through your pride and your hardness of neck — were banished; you went out from the lordship of God who created you; you destroyed yourself.

13.text: “That his Godhead’s praise might not be lacking, God by the counsel of his will created the one who praises him. Know that his praise shall not be lacking.

14.text: “For he knows all before it is done; he knew that you would break his commandment before he created you. Before the world was made, the counsel was hidden with him; when you denied him, he created his servant Adam in his image and likeness.

15.text: “As Solomon said: ’Before the hills he begot me; before the world was made firm; before the foundation of the earth was laid;

16.text: “’before the prop of mountains and hills was planted; before the way of the world was established; before the light of sun and moon shone; before the food of stars and seasons was known;

17.text: “’before night and day alternated; before the sea was bounded with sand; before all created creation was created;

18.text: “‘before all that is seen today was seen; before all the name that is called today was called — he begot me.’ So also, you and the angels like you, and his servant Adam, were within the consciousness of God.

19.text: “When you denied [him], that his holy name might be praised — that he might be praised in his servant Adam who was humbled, whom he created from earth — when you exalted yourself, he created Adam.

20.text: “For God hears the prayer of the poor from afar; God loves the praise of humbled people.

21.text: “God disregards the matter of the proud; he does not love the strength of the horse; he is not glad in the strength of a man.

22.text: “But God is glad in those who fear him and cry out weeping for their sin.

23.text: “You — you could not confess in repentance.

24.text: “But that earthly one [Adam], weeping greatly before God for his sin, returned in repentance.

25.text: “You — in the pride of your heart and the hardness of your neck — did not know the way of peace; you did not know repentance; in repentance, weeping, and tears you could not confess before your Creator God.

26.text: “But that poor one of ash and earth returned with weeping and tears to the way of repentance, peace, and humility.

27.text: “You — to God who created you, you did not humble yourself or the inner husk of your heart.

28.text: “But he, having transgressed his transgression, humbled himself and confessed; he did not exalt himself.

29.text: “And that error — he did not create it; it came from you. You created the crime and brought it out; in your pride, you took him with you to your destruction.

30.text: “For he knew both of you before he created you; he knew your walk; he knows that this was done in the pride of your heart.

31.text: “But that one — without the cunning of pride — he returned through repentance, weeping, and tears.

32.text: “You — in the pride of your heart — could not confess in repentance. The man who sins and does not confess in repentance makes his sin worse than his former transgression.

33.text: “But the man who sins and confesses and weeps before his Creator God — he has truly repented; that he might soften his Lord’s heart, he has found the way of salvation; before his Lord he confesses; his Lord eases what he had counseled to be angry over the servant; in much repentance and prostration he has confessed; his former sin is forgiven.

34.text: “If he does not return to his previous transgression — if he does this — this is complete repentance. And Adam did not forget remembering his Creator and confessing to his Creator.

35.text: “You also — confess to your Creator in repentance; multiply not transgression against him and against the work of his hand. For they are flesh and blood; God who created them knows their weakness.

36.text: “After their soul is separated, their flesh becomes dust until the day God shall please.”

1.text: Know your Creator; do not forget the Holy One of Israel who has strengthened you and saved you. When you were earth, he created you in his image and likeness — that you might be glad, he set you in Paradise to till the ground.

2.text: When you transgressed his commandment, he brought you out from Paradise into this land cursed for your sake, which brings forth bramble and thorn.

3.text: For you are earth, and she is earth; you are dust, and she is dust; you are ground, and she is ground. From her you eat; to her you return; you become dust until he wills to raise you. For he shall examine all the iniquity and sin you have done.

4.text: Know what you shall answer in that time. Remember the evil and good you have done in this world; weigh and consider whether the evil is greater or the good is greater.

5.text: If you have multiplied good, it shall be well with you, that you may rejoice and exult on the day the dead rise.

6.text: But if you have multiplied evil, woe to you! As your hands’ work and your heart’s wickedness, you shall receive your recompense — as you have done evil to your neighbor, as you have not feared God — as your work, you shall receive your recompense.

7.text: If you have betrayed your neighbor — if you have sworn falsely in the name of God — as your work, you shall receive your recompense.

8.text: Pretending to your neighbor, you make your false word seem true; but you yourself know that you have spoken falsehood.

9.text: Convincing those with you, you firm up your word as truth; you multiply what is not true; as your work, you shall receive your recompense. Saying “I will give you what I do not give,” you betray your neighbor.

10.text: When in pure heart you said “I will give,” demons surround you like dogs; they make you forget all things; whether you rise to give or wish to give — the wealth of this world makes you covet, that you may fatten yourself on wealth which does not profit you and which you cannot eat. For he has said: “They gather; and do not know for whom they gather.”

11.text: Again — “the lying sons of Adam make the balance false; they go always from vanity to vanity” — as he has said.

12.text: O people — by tampering with the balance and the weight-stone; by stealing the wealth of others and by violence adding to your own wealth; by trespassing on your neighbor’s property and field; by making for yourselves the profit that does not belong to your neighbor — do not place your hope in violence.

13.text: If you do this, as your work you shall receive.

14.text: O people — eat fittingly by the work of your hand; do not trust in plunder. By unfitting, judgment-less seizing and snatching, do not love to eat another’s wealth.

15.text: Though you eat it, it does not satisfy you; though you fatten on it, in the time of your death you leave it to another; it does not profit you.

16.text: Though your wealth abounds, do not be proud in mind. The wealth of sinners is like the smoke from a furnace which the wind takes; a little wealth in truth is better than much wealth of sinners.

1.text: Remember the day of your death; when your souls are separated from your bodies, when you leave your wealth to another, when you go to a way you do not know — think of what comes upon you.

2.text: Those who receive you are evil; in form they are misshapen; in their fierceness they terrify; they do not hear your word, and you do not hear their word.

3.text: Because you did not do the will of God your God, when you petition them, they do not answer you; for this reason they terrify you greatly.

4.text: Demons fear them — but to people who fulfill God’s will, there is no fear in them. The demons mock the souls of sinners.

5.text: Because they despised this world — for this greatly gladdens them — the souls of righteous people rejoice at the chant of angels. But the souls of sinners — evil angels receive them.

6.text: To settle the souls of the righteous, angels of mercy are sent from God; they receive the souls of the righteous and good. But evil demons receive the souls of sinners — sent from the Devil that they may mock the souls of sinners.

7.text: Sinners, woe to you! Before the day of your death reaches you, weep for yourselves; after your death, the time that has passed does not return.

8.text: Rather, before your time has passed — while you are still here — enter repentance, that when you arrive before God’s face you may dwell without affliction and without disease, in joy.

9.text: Lest the worthless will that estranges you from God draw you away — let there not be found in you sharp reproach and luxurious living, the love of food and pleasure. For a body sated beyond measure does not remember the name of God; rather the spirit of the Devil dwells in it, not the spirit of life.

10.text: As Moses said: “Jacob ate and was satisfied; he grew fat, he grew thick, he grew broad; he abandoned God who created him;

11.text: and his life departed from God.” For unmeasured gorging of the belly is to be like an untamed horse; for unmeasured eating and drinking and adultery is to be like a wild pig of the desert.

12.text: But the one who eats with measure is firm on the foundation of God; like the cornerstone, like a fortified wall, he stands firm. For it is said: “The sinner flees when no one pursues him.”

13.text: But the righteous lives bounding like a lion.

14.text: But people who do not love God do not keep his word; their mind is not straight.

15.text: And God — that, while they are on earth, they may not rest — by trembling and fear, by the seizing of their wealth, by countless many afflictions held — bound in chains from the hand of their lords —

16.text: lest they be at rest from the affliction, lest their dwelling be in peace, in various terrifying afflictions, brings sorrow and panic upon them.

1.text: As David said: “In God I have trusted; I will not fear; what shall man do to me?” — In people who trust in God there is no fear or panic.

2.text: Again he said: “Though warriors should surround me, in him I trusted; one thing I asked of God; that I seek; he who trusted in him shall live forever; from evil he shall not fear.”

3.text: Who is the man who trusted in God and was put to shame? Who is the one God has called and rejected?

4.text: “Those who love me, I will love; those who honor me, I will honor; those who turn to me, I will keep” — he has said. Who is the man who has hoped in him and been put to shame?

5.text: Save the body of the widow; from all who oppose you with evil, save them — that God may save you. Protect them; after you, he shall protect your children. For the children of the righteous are blessed; they give from their excess; they do not lack grain.

1.text: Job trusted in God; for he did not neglect to praise God his Creator — [God] saved him from all the affliction the Devil, enemy of the sons of Adam, brought upon him. In the affliction that came upon him, he did not grieve his heart. Rather he said: “The LORD gave; the LORD has taken; the LORD has done as he wished; in all things, in heaven and earth, let the name of the LORD be praised.”

2.text: When God saw that Job’s heart was pure, God received him with much glory.

3.text: He gave him wealth more abundant than his former wealth; for he had become very patient — because he endured all the affliction that came upon him, he healed him of his wound.

4.text: So also you — if you endure the enemies sent to you, you become blessed.

5.text: Endure! Lest because of the affliction that has come upon you from people who hate you, you grieve your mind — that, for you and after you for your children and your children’s children, he may be a refuge to you.

6.text: Trust him; he shall be your refuge. Call upon him; he shall hear you. Hope in him; he shall pardon you. Petition him; he shall be a father to you.

7.text: Remember Esther and Mordecai, Judith and Gideon, Barak and Deborah, Samson and Jephthah —

8.text: and others like them, who hardened themselves to trust in God; whose enemies did not overcome them.

9.text: For God is true; he does not show partiality of face. Those who chose to do evil against them — they received evil. But all those who fear him and do righteousness — he keeps their souls; he gives them honor and intimacy.

10.text: In their going in and coming out, in their death and their life, in their sitting and their rising — he gladdens them. For he saves and he kills.

1.text: Whether in heaven or on earth, whether the subtle or the solid — all is his; all by his ordinance stands and abides.

2.text: None transgresses the law and commandment of the Creator of the whole world; the path of the eagle that flies in heaven — to where he wills, he commands his going.

3.text: The way of the serpent in the rock — where he wills, he commands him. The way of a ship in the midst of the sea — none knows its way except God alone.

4.text: Whether the soul of the righteous or the soul of the sinner, after she is separated from her flesh — none knows the way the soul takes except God alone.

5.text: Whether she goes around in the wilderness or on the mountain — who knows where she goes? Whether she flies like a bird; whether she descends upon the cleft of the mountain; whether she becomes like the dew of Hermon;

6.text: whether she becomes like the whirlwind; whether she becomes like lightning that straightens her path;

7.text: whether she becomes like the stars that shine over the deep; whether she becomes like the sand of the seashore heaped in the midst of the deep;

8.text: whether she becomes like the cornerstone fixed on the edge of the sea’s depth; whether she becomes like a tree planted by the water-channels that gives lovely fruit;

9.text: whether the sun’s heat burns her, and the wind picks her up and carries her to another place where she does not sprout — whose trace is not found, becoming like grass; whose trace is not found, becoming like mist of urine — who knows?

10.text: Who knows the way of God? Who are his counselors? With whom does he take counsel?

11.text: For the thought of God is hidden from man; who pursues his trace?

12.text: Who can examine God’s counsel and his wisdom? For he founded the earth on the water; he established her without a peg; in his complete wisdom, he firmed up the heaven on the wind; he stretched out the male-water [oceans] like a tent.

13.text: And he commanded the clouds to rain rain upon the earth; he causes grass to grow, and countless fruits — that they might be food for man, that we might rejoice in God together.

14.text: God gives to the sons of men all his blessing, his joy, and his satisfaction — this is that they may be sated and praise God who gave them from the fruit of the earth.

15.text: The lovely garment he has put on them; all the desired blessing; the joy and gladness given to those who fulfill the will of God — he gives them.

16.text: And to those who keep the commandment of God — in the dwelling he prepared for their fathers in heaven — he gives glory and beloved-ness and gladness.

17.text: To those who lived in his worship and his judgment — who kept his law and sought his ordinance, who kept and provided for them, who raised and honored them, who did not depart from his commandment — he gives glory and grace. And I — by causing their enemies to weaken, by guarding their bodies — saw what God does for his beloved in this world.

18.text: All things, as they ask, he gives them, and fulfills their will. Do not depart from God’s commandment; fulfill the will of God.

19.text: Lest he be angry with you, lest in one moment he destroy you, lest in his wrath he strike you, lest you go out from the inheritance of your fathers where you formerly were, lest your dwelling forever be Gehenna where there is no exit — do not depart from his commandment and his law.

20.text: When you stand before God, that your work may be good — while your soul is not separated from your flesh — keep the will of God your Creator.

21.text: For the kingdom of heaven and earth is his alone; almighty power and kingship are his; mercy and pardon are his alone.

22.text: He makes rich; he makes poor; he humbles; he honors.

23.text: And David said concerning him: “Man is like vanity; his days pass like a shadow.

24.text: “O Lord, but you abide forever; the calling of your name is to generation upon generation.”

25.text: Again he said: “Your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom; your rule is to generation upon generation” — you have taken kingship from Saul and given it to David.

26.text: But you — there is no one who appoints you; there is no one able to depose you; there is no one able to see you; but you — you see all.

27.text: Your kingdom — for generation upon generation, forever, is not deposed; there is none who rules him; but he — he rules all; sees all.

28.text: That they may praise him without doubt and with straight mind know his worship — that they may not be those who, instead of God alone who created them, provided for them, honored them, raised them — bow down to other gods — for he created man in his image and likeness; he examines heart and reins.

29.text: But they refuse to worship God who created them; to stone and wood, and to silver and gold made by human hand, they bow down.

30.text: And they sacrifice to them, until the smoke of their sacrifice rises to heaven there to stand before God; he shall accuse them of all the sin they have done in their idolatry.

31.text: They did not keep the commandment of God they had been taught. Rather they learned idol-worship, every defiling work that is not fitting; astrology and divination and idolatry; evil will and every work God does not love.

32.text: That they might be praised in the presence of God and his angels — that they might save their bodies from sin and iniquity — because they did not love to praise God — for lack of good work they do all this.

33.text: When all together are raised from the tomb where they were buried and where their bones decayed, their soul stands naked before God; the soul shall dwell in the houses of light prepared for the good.

34.text: But the soul of sinners shall dwell in darkness. When the tombs open, the bodies rise; the souls return to the bodies from which they were first separated.

35.text: Naked, as they were born naked, they stand before God; the sin they have done from their infancy unto that time shall be revealed.

36.text: They shall bear their sin on their shoulder; whether little or much sin they have done, as they have done, so they shall receive.

1.text: If you have not believed the resurrection of the dead, hear how, in winter, unborn souls rise; for the Spirit of God, breathed upon them as before, rests upon them.

2.text: And to die, by his word, he commanded them aforetime.

3.text: Their flesh decaying, as he wills they rise; again they are renewed.

4.text: Again, when rain falls and saturates the earth, they rise; as was prepared from of old, they live.

5.text: Those that live by living-soul; all that moves on earth, and all that water brings forth — he commanded, and they were created. For the Spirit of God hovered over the water; by his Spirit and his word he gives them living-soul.

6.text: You blind-of-heart, who say “the dead do not rise” — look: by his Spirit and his word, without father and mother, they are created. If you have wisdom, how do you say that the dead are not raised by the word of God their Creator?

7.text: Repent, and return to your faith. For the dead — who in the grave have become ash and dust — by the word of God shall rise.

8.text: As his word formerly said, by the dew of pardon from God they rise; that word, encompassing all, raises the dead as he wills.

9.text: Know that, raised, you shall stand before him; do not think according to your thought that you remain in the grave.

10.text: It is not so — but as you have done on earth, whether good or evil, raised, you shall receive your wage; for it is the day of recompense.

11.text: At the resurrection, in all the sin you have done, you shall receive your recompense; from your infancy to that time, the written debt of yours you shall complete; you have no excuse — as in the work of this world — by which to deny your sin.

12.text: As you make your false word seem true to your face, as you make the false thing you have spoken seem true — there you have no excuse by which to plead.

13.text: For she [the soul] — knowing all the evil you have done — shall reveal you before God her Creator; for the word of God dwelling in you shall speak against you.

14.text: And there, for the sin you have done, you shall be ashamed. That you may be praised with those who are praised for their good work — not be ashamed on the day of judgment before the angels and people — hasten here to enter into repentance before you arrive there.

15.text: Those who praise God with the angels receive their wage from their Creator without shame; they are glad. But while you are alive in your flesh, if you have not done good work, you have no portion with the righteous.

16.text: When you had knowledge — when you had wage and market — you did not prepare yourself. When you had wealth, you did not give a morsel to the hungry — worthless repentance shall be yours.

17.text: When you had clothing, you did not clothe the naked; when you had authority, you did not save the oppressed.

18.text: When you had knowledge, you did not teach the sinner — that he might return and enter repentance; that God might forgive the sin he had done in ignorance. When you had strength, with which to overcome — you did not fight the demons who war against you.

19.text: When you had firmness, that you might weaken the strength of your infancy that is in flesh, that you might subject yourself to righteousness, not to please the flesh in the world — you did not fast; you did not pray.

20.text: Not in worldly joy, in sweet foods and excellent drink — not in fine clothing or adornment with gold and silver —

21.text: not in honored gems of India, in topaz and emerald: this is not the fitting adornment of man.

22.text: For man — his adornment is purity, wisdom, and knowledge; without jealousy and without envy; without doubt and without quarrel; loving one another fittingly.

23.text: Loving your neighbor as yourself, not returning evil for evil to the man who has done evil to you — that you may enter into the dwelling given to those who have endured affliction; that, with those who have inherited the holy land by patience and knowledge, hoping for the Kingdom of Heaven at the resurrection, your wage may be given to you.

24.text: “After we die, we shall not rise” — do not say this. For the Devil makes those who say and think this lose hope, that at the resurrection they may not be saved. When the resurrection has reached them, they shall know. People who have done sin in ignorance — at the resurrection they shall utterly grieve, because they did not believe that on that day they would rise. He shall hold their sin against them.

25.text: Therefore, for the work they did on earth — for its evil — they shall be reproached; the resurrection by which they rise in flesh together — which they denied — they shall see.

26.text: Because they did not order their work well, they shall weep then. If they could — that they might not be those who weep there — if they had wept in this world, it would have been better for them.

27.text: If here, by our will, we do not weep — there, against our will, they shall make us weep. If here we do not prepare repentance — there, worthless and unprofitable shouting and weeping we shall prepare.

28.text: That you may pass over from death to life — from this passing world to the Kingdom of Heaven above — from this earthly light to the heavenly light — prepare good work.

29.text: That with the people who believe the resurrection of the dead, in the Kingdom of Heaven in unending joy, you may be glad — refuse the joy that is on earth. From today and unto eternity. Amen.
